methods.name: to_dict
methods.summary: Return the config as the JSON-ready dict `adapter_config.json` holds.
methods.extended:
Enums become their strings and sets of module names sorted lists,
so the result goes straight to `json.dumps` and back through
`from_dict`.  A field the reference's config of this method lacks
(`IA3Config.layers_to_transform`) is written only when it is set,
so a file that does not use it is one the reference reads too.

returns.description: One entry per field, keyed by the reference's field names.

examples:
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig
>>> d = LoraConfig(target_modules=["v", "q"], task_type="CAUSAL_LM").to_dict()
>>> d["target_modules"], d["task_type"], d["peft_type"]
(['q', 'v'], 'CAUSAL_LM', 'LORA')

methods.name: from_dict
methods.summary: Build a config from a dict such as a parsed `adapter_config.json`.
methods.extended:
The constructor cannot do this: a file from the reference carries
keys v1 has no field for.  Such a key is accepted only at a value
that turns its feature off — null, false or empty
(`"loftq_config": {}`, `"megatron_config": null`) — and dropped (with
a warning if v1 does not know the key); at any other value it
raises, as it would change what the adapter computes.  The
`peft_version` provenance key is dropped.  Called on
`PeftConfig`, the dict's `peft_type` picks the class.

parameters.name: config_dict
parameters.description: The config's fields, by the reference's names.

returns.description: The validated config, of the class the dict's method names.

raises.description:
The dict describes another adapter type, or turns on a feature
v1 lacks.

examples:
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig
>>> config = LoraConfig.from_dict(
...     {"peft_type": "LORA", "r": 4, "target_modules": ["c_attn"],
...      "use_dora": False, "loftq_config": {}, "peft_version": "0.17.0"})
>>> config.r, config.target_modules
(4, {'c_attn'})

methods.name: save_pretrained
methods.summary: Write `adapter_config.json` into `save_directory`.
methods.extended:
The file is the reference's: `to_dict` with its keys sorted,
indented by two spaces.  The directory is created if missing.

parameters.name: save_directory
parameters.description: Directory to write into.

raises.description: `save_directory` names an existing file.

examples:
>>> import tempfile
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
...     LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["fc"]).save_pretrained(d)
...     LoraConfig.from_pretrained(d).r

methods.name: from_json_file
methods.summary: Read a config file into the dict it holds, unchanged but for `runtime_config`.
methods.extended:
What `from_pretrained` reads before it chooses a config class: the
file's content as a dict, as the reference's `from_json_file` returns
it.  `from_dict` turns it into a config.

parameters.name: path_json_file
parameters.description: The path of a JSON file such as `adapter_config.json`.

returns.description:
The file's object, without a `runtime_config` key: the
reference warns that such a key is ignored, since a runtime
configuration is valid at runtime only.

raises.description: There is no file at `path_json_file`.
The file does not hold a JSON object.

examples:
>>> import os, tempfile
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, PeftConfig
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
...     LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["fc"]).save_pretrained(d)
...     raw = PeftConfig.from_json_file(os.path.join(d, "adapter_config.json"))
>>> raw["peft_type"], raw["r"]
('LORA', 2)

methods.name: from_pretrained
methods.signature: from_pretrained(pretrained_model_name_or_path: str | os.PathLike[str], subfolder: str | None = None)
methods.summary: Read `adapter_config.json` from a local adapter directory.
methods.extended:
The file's `peft_type` picks the config class: called on
`PeftConfig` this returns a `LoraConfig` for a LoRA adapter,
and called on a method's own class it refuses the file of another
method.

parameters.name: pretrained_model_name_or_path
parameters.description:
A directory holding `adapter_config.json` — one written by
`save_pretrained` or by the reference library.  Hub ids
are not resolved; download the adapter first.

parameters.name: subfolder
parameters.description:
A directory under `pretrained_model_name_or_path` that holds
the file, e.g. the sub-directory `save_pretrained` gives each
adapter but the one named `"default"`.

raises.description: The directory has no `adapter_config.json`.
The file does not hold a JSON object.

examples:
>>> import tempfile
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
...     LoraConfig(r=16, lora_alpha=32, target_modules="all-linear").save_pretrained(d)
...     loaded = LoraConfig.from_pretrained(d)
>>> loaded.r, loaded.lora_alpha, loaded.target_modules
(16, 32, 'all-linear')

members.summary: How `lucid.peft.get_peft_model` adapts a model with VB-LoRA.
members.extended:
VB-LoRA (Li et al., 2024, [arXiv:2405.15179](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15179) — Vector Bank LoRA) builds every
low-rank factor of every layer out of one shared **vector bank**
$V \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times b}$ of $N$ vectors of length $b$.
The factors $A \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_{in}}$ and
$B \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{out} \times r}$ are cut into sub-vectors of length
$b$; each sub-vector is a softmax-weighted mix of the top-$k$
bank vectors picked by learned logits,

$$
\mathrm{softmax}(\ell_{ij})_t\, V_t,
\qquad y = W x + b + B A\,x ,
$$

so the trainable parameters are the logits $\ell$ and the bank, shared by
the whole model.  The adapter does **not** start as the base: both factors are
non-zero from the first step (as in the paper).

Field names, defaults and `adapter_config.json` are the reference
adapter library's.  Every field is keyword-only.

parameters.name: task_type
parameters.description: The task the adapter is for (metadata; see `TaskType`).

parameters.name: peft_type
parameters.description:
The method; filled in by the subclass when omitted, refused when
it names another.

parameters.name: auto_mapping
parameters.description:
The class of the base model, `{"base_model_class": name,
"parent_library": module}` — what `AutoPeftModel*` rebuilds the
base with.  `PeftModel.save_pretrained` writes it.

parameters.name: base_model_name_or_path
parameters.description: Name of the model the adapter was trained on (metadata).

parameters.name: revision
parameters.description: Revision of that model (metadata).

parameters.name: inference_mode
parameters.description: Freeze the adapter too, for inference.

parameters.name: target_modules
parameters.description:
The `nn.Linear` modules to adapt, matched as `LoraConfig.target_modules`
is.  `None` takes the default for the base model's `model_type`
(`VBLORA_DEFAULT_TARGET_MODULES` in `lucid.peft.tuners.vblora._defaults`);
another model type raises `ValueError`.

parameters.name: exclude_modules
parameters.description: Modules never adapted, matched like `target_modules`.

parameters.name: modules_to_save
parameters.description: Modules trained in full beside the adapter (a classifier head).

parameters.name: layers_to_transform
parameters.description: As in `LoraConfig`.

parameters.name: layers_pattern
parameters.description: As in `LoraConfig`.

parameters.name: r
parameters.description: Rank of the factors.

parameters.name: num_vectors
parameters.description: Vectors in the bank ($N$); use more for bigger models.

parameters.name: vector_length
parameters.description:
Length $b$ of a bank vector; every targeted layer's input and output size
must be a multiple of it.

parameters.name: topk
parameters.description:
How many bank vectors mix into a sub-vector ($k$).  `2` is the paper's
recommendation; larger values make the saved model bigger.

parameters.name: save_only_topk_weights
parameters.description:
Write only each sub-vector's top-$k$ indices and weights instead of the
logits.  The file is much smaller and good for inference or merging, not for
resuming training.

parameters.name: vblora_dropout
parameters.description: Dropout on the update's input, in `[0, 1)`.

parameters.name: fan_in_fan_out
parameters.description:
For bases that store their weight `(in, out)`.  `nn.Linear` does not,
so `True` warns and is reset to `False`.

parameters.name: bias
parameters.description:
The reference also offers `"all"` and `"vblora_only"`; here the adapter
trains its own tensors only, and those raise `NotImplementedError`.

parameters.name: init_vector_bank_bound
parameters.description: The bank starts uniform in `[-bound, bound]` (not zero, or the gradients vanish).

parameters.name: init_logits_std
parameters.description: The logits start normal with this standard deviation.

raises.description: A field holds a value of the wrong type.
A field is out of range, or `topk` exceeds `num_vectors`.
`bias` is not `"none"`.

examples:
>>> from lucid.peft.tuners.vblora import VBLoRAConfig
>>> config = VBLoRAConfig(r=4, num_vectors=60, vector_length=64, target_modules=["q", "v"])
>>> sorted(config.target_modules), config.peft_type
(['q', 'v'], <PeftType.VBLORA: 'VBLORA'>)
>>> VBLoRAConfig.from_dict(config.to_dict()) == config
True

members.name: Linear
members.summary: An `nn.Linear` with a VB-LoRA update: $y = W x + b + B\,A\,\mathrm{drop}(x)$.

parameters.name: base_layer
parameters.description: The layer to adapt; the other parameters are those of `VBLoRALayer`.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: Name of the adapter created at once.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description: The adapter's config.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft.tuners.vblora import Linear, VBLoRAConfig
>>> base = nn.Linear(8, 4)
>>> config = VBLoRAConfig(r=2, num_vectors=6, vector_length=4, target_modules=["x"])
>>> layer = Linear(base, "default", config)
>>> tuple(layer.vblora_logits_A["default"].shape), tuple(layer.vblora_logits_B["default"].shape)
((2, 2, 6), (1, 2, 6))
>>> tuple(layer.vblora_vector_bank["default"].shape)
(6, 4)
>>> tuple(layer(lucid.randn(3, 8)).shape)
(3, 4)

The names this layer holds nothing for are skipped by the forward

methods.name: merge
methods.signature: merge(safe_merge: bool = False, adapter_names: list[str] | None = None)
methods.summary: Fold the update into the base weights, in place.
methods.extended:
The weights keep their identity — they are written, not replaced —
so whatever holds them (an optimizer, a tied embedding) sees the
merged values.  That is also why a weight shared with another
module must not be merged into; the tuner's `merge_adapter` and
`merge_and_unload` refuse it, as this layer alone cannot see the
rest of the model.

parameters.name: safe_merge
parameters.description:
Check the merged weights for NaN / inf first and leave the base
untouched if there are any.

parameters.name: adapter_names
parameters.description: Adapters to merge; the active ones this layer holds by default.

raises.description:
An adapter name this layer does not hold, or `safe_merge`
found a non-finite merged weight.

The adapter is disabled, or the layer's own rules refuse the merge
(`lora_bias` on a base with no bias).
This layer's update cannot be written into its base weights.

methods.name: unmerge
methods.summary: Take every merged update back out of the base weights, in place.
methods.extended:
The result equals the original weights up to the rounding of the
round trip.

methods.name: update_layer

The adapter is built whole before the layer holds any of it.  A layer
that holds an adapter already keeps applying the adapters it applied:
the new one is inactive until `set_adapter` names it; a layer with
none starts applying this one.

A merged model runs at the base model's cost; `unmerge_adapter`
takes the updates out again.  Every refusal is made before any
weight is written: nothing is merged if a layer's base weight is
shared with another module (a tied LM head — merging would change
that module too) or if the adapter is disabled.

methods.name: merge_and_unload
methods.signature: merge_and_unload(progressbar: bool = False, safe_merge: bool = False, adapter_names: list[str] | None = None)
methods.summary: Merge the adapters into the base weights and return the plain model.
methods.extended:
Each adapter layer is replaced by its merged base module — the base
model's own module, holding its own `Parameter` objects — and each
`modules_to_save` entry by the active adapter's trained copy (the
original when that adapter has none).  Adapters not merged are
dropped with their layers.  Every base parameter gets back the
`requires_grad` it had before injection.

raises.description:
A base weight is shared with another module, or a
`modules_to_save` module shared one (its trained copy would
break the tie).

methods.name: unload
methods.summary: Remove every adapter without merging and return the original model.
methods.extended:
Every adapter layer is replaced by the module it wrapped (a merged
one is unmerged first), every `modules_to_save` entry by its
original module, and every base parameter gets back the
`requires_grad` it had before injection.

members.summary: A model with VB-LoRA layers put into it, the vector bank they share, and the tools to take them out.
members.extended:
Construction replaces each `nn.Linear` `config` selects with a VB-LoRA
layer around it and freezes every other parameter.  The model is changed in
place and kept as `model`; a public name this wrapper lacks is read from
it.  `config` itself is not changed: `peft_config` holds a copy with the
default `target_modules` spelled out.

The vector bank is one `(num_vectors, vector_length)` parameter per adapter,
held here as `vblora_vector_bank` (the reference's attribute) and trained
with the layers' logits.  Every layer reads it from there; the first layer
holds it in its module tree, so a state dict lists it once and the adapter
file holds one bank.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: The model to adapt.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description: What to adapt and how.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: Name of the adapter, the key in every `vblora_logits_*` and in the bank.

raises.description:
No module matches `target_modules`, a match is not an `nn.Linear`,
a match's sizes are not multiples of `vector_length`, or
`modules_to_save` matches nothing.
The model already holds adapter layers of another method.

examples:
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft.tuners.vblora import VBLoRAConfig, VBLoRAModel
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(8, 8), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(8, 4))
>>> config = VBLoRAConfig(r=2, num_vectors=6, vector_length=4, target_modules=["0", "2"])
>>> vblora = VBLoRAModel(net, config)
>>> tuple(vblora.vblora_vector_bank["default"].shape)
(6, 4)
>>> net[0].base_layer.weight.requires_grad, vblora.vblora_vector_bank["default"].requires_grad
(False, True)
>>> vblora.unload() is net, type(net[0]) is nn.Linear
(True, True)

summary: `lucid.peft.tuners.vblora` — VB-LoRA: low-rank factors mixed from one shared vector bank.
extended:
VB-LoRA (Li et al., 2024, [arXiv:2405.15179](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15179) — Vector Bank LoRA) cuts the LoRA factors of every layer
into sub-vectors and builds each as a softmax-weighted mix of the top-$k$ vectors of a single
bank shared by the whole model; the learned logits that pick and weight them, and the bank, are the
trained parameters.  The adapter stores logits and a bank, not per-layer factors, so it holds far
fewer numbers than LoRA's.  Unlike LoRA it does not start as the base.  Pick it when storage per
adapter is the constraint.

Where the reference library keeps them, so `isinstance(m, VBLoRALayer)` and `from
lucid.peft.tuners.vblora import VBLoRAConfig, Linear` read as they do there.  One layer type for
the one module the method adapts, `nn.Linear`.  `VBLoRAConfig` and `VBLoRAModel` (which holds
the bank) are here and exported from `lucid.peft`.  Importing the package registers the method
(its config under `PeftType.VBLORA`, its tuner and layer), which is what makes `get_peft_model`
and `PeftModel.from_pretrained` know it.
citation: Li, Yang, et al. "VB-LoRA: Extreme Parameter Efficient Fine-Tuning with Vector Banks." [arXiv:2405.15179](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15179), 2024.
theory:
VB-LoRA (Li et al., 2024, [arXiv:2405.15179](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15179) — Vector Bank LoRA) builds every
low-rank factor of every layer out of one shared **vector bank**
$V \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times b}$ of $N$ vectors of length $b$.
The factors $A \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_{in}}$ and
$B \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{out} \times r}$ are cut into sub-vectors of length
$b$; each sub-vector is a softmax-weighted mix of the top-$k$
bank vectors picked by learned logits,

$$
\mathrm{softmax}(\ell_{ij})_t\, V_t,
\qquad y = W x + b + B A\,x ,
$$
